item.title: Remotely operated message signs installed in outback WA
item.description: The new electronic signs provide road condition information in real-time. Image: Shire of Carnarvon The Shire of Carnarvon has installed new electronic variable message signs along Minilya–Lyndon Road and the Quobba–Gnaraloo Road network. According to the council, the new remote operated signs were installed to help improve safety, traveller communication, and response capability across its vast road network. item.title: Volvo lifts the lid on its new low-horsepower 13 litre engine range
item.description: Peak torque starts at 905Nm and stretches to 1400Nm across the three new variants. Image: Volvo Trucks Australia Volvo’s popular Euro 6 13-litre engine platform has a new range of horsepower ratings available for the versatile FM model. Ranging from 380hp and 1850Nm to 420hp and 2100Nm, as well as a 460hp/2300Nm variant, the new range is intended to provide robust and efficient powertrain options across a range of transport applications. item.title: Mobile phone and seatbelt cameras widen net in NSW
item.description: An animation of the mobile phone and seatbelt cameras shows how the enforcement system will now work. Image: TfNSW Truckies driving through NSW have been warned that the state's transportable mobile phone and seatbelt cameras will begin operating at their full capacity from Sunday, March 1. Until now they only checked up to two lanes of traffic travelling in one direction, but from this weekend will switch to bi-directional coverage on single lane roads. item.title: Tyres by the kilometre: Why fleet buying has changed
item.description: The Giti GSR256 is a steer tyre, engineered for durability, mileage, and reliable performance in highway and regional applications. Image: Giti In Australian trucking, tyres are no longer judged by brand recognition or sticker price. They are judged by one thing above all else: cost per kilometre. How evenly a tyre wears, how long the casing lasts, and how many kilometres it achieves now matter far more than what logo is stamped on the sidewall. item.title: Truckies fed up over misuse of parking bays
item.description: Drivers are complaining that some companies are misusing rest bays as depots, conducting roadside repairs and disposing of oil and tyres. Image: Helen Keese Trouble is brewing between some Western Australian truckies over the widespread misuse of roadside parking bays around Kalgoorlie.
